info.title: narrator
info.description: Self-hosted TTS book reader. One global session: the server holds one book, one chapter and one playhead across every client, which is why anything cacheable is scoped by ?book= and positions can be written by name. No auth, no TLS, wildcard CORS - it assumes a private machine reached over Tailscale.

get.description:
This is the streaming path: iOS plays it natively in a plain `<audio>`, so the
OS owns buffering and segment retry — a blip re-fetches one six-second segment
instead of killing the whole load. The m4a stays the download format, because
native HLS bypasses the service worker and can never be the offline one.

post.summary:
Parse an EPUB and make it the session's book. Also writes `plan.json` and the
text bundle, both rebuilt from scratch: re-parsing can move chunk boundaries,
and a stale shard would put every position in it on the wrong words.

400.description: the file is not a readable EPUB

200.description: filed - the outbox may delete its copy

400.description: no book, no audio, or nothing heard

500.description: transcription or the vault write failed

post.summary: Select a chapter and start rendering from a given chunk.
post.description:
The opened chunk is *guaranteed* to render: the worker renders whatever is
under the playhead before anything else, and this sets the playhead.

post.summary:
Pause playback. The time you are *not* listening is exactly when the buffer
should grow, so this stops audio, not the renderer — unless
`PREFETCH_WHILE_PAUSED=0`.

Report the playhead. Drags `render_idx` forward on a forward jump, never
backwards — anything already on disk still plays, and the worker skips files
that exist, so nothing is re-rendered.
Record a position for a *named* book without loading it.
post.description:
This is what the offline queue pushes on reconnect, possibly for a book the
server has since swapped out. Last write wins, which is the right rule for one
reader on several devices. Fields not supplied are kept from the existing
record.

post.summary:
The old "render ahead N hours" target. Its UI is gone — the chapter manager
replaced it — but the endpoint stays for the CLI and anything else pointed
at it.
Explicitly stop/start the render worker, independent of playback.

the whole book is readable with no network and no rendered audio; cache none
and the reader still lists it.

ApiError.description:
Every error body in this API: `{"error": "..."}`, and nothing else. The
reader's `get()` reads exactly this field.

path.description: Absolute path on the server — what `/api/load` takes back.

building.description: Complete and handed to the packer now.

rendering.description: Not complete; queued for rendering first.

shard.description:
Which shard holds this chapter's words. Omitted entirely by `/api/load`,
always a number in `book.json` — never `null`, which is why the schema
overrides utoipa's default nullable-because-Option rendering.

m4a.description:
Whether a *trustworthy* packed m4a exists. A manifest whose `chunks`
disagrees with the plan reports false: it points at the wrong words.

queued.description:
Always present: a row only exists for a loaded book, and then the
chapter manager's three flags always have an answer.

rendered.description: How many of this chapter's chunks are on disk.

force.description: `/api/chapters/build` only: rebuild even if an m4a already exists.

pack.description: `/api/chapters/render` only: also pack each chapter as it completes.

paras.description:
What lets the reader re-form real paragraphs from chunks. Additive:
existing clients (the Obsidian plugin) only read title + chunks.

building.description:
Absent only in the "no book loaded" shape; `null` when nothing is being
packed. The python server distinguishes those two and the reader's type
says `building?: number | null`, so the nesting is the contract.

key.description: The cache directory name: the file stem, truncated to 50 characters.

oneOf.description: The stored position for this book, or null if it has never been opened.

starts.description:
`starts[i]` is chunk `i`'s start second. `currentTime` maps back by
bisecting this.

chapter.description: Where the memo was recorded. Defaults to the session's own position.

file.description: The note's file name in the vault.

Ok2.description: `{"ok": true}` plus whatever else a handler wants to say.

still_rendering.description: Whether the renderer keeps filling the buffer while playback is stopped.

Position.description:
One book's last position. Field order is the python dict's, because it is the
order `json.dumps` writes and the file is diffed by git.

hours.description:
Hours of estimated audio to build ahead. 0 or null falls back to the
static `PRERENDER_CHAPTERS`.

packing.description: Chapters that were already complete and went straight to the packer.

paras.description:
What lets the reader re-form real paragraphs from chunks — a wall of
one-sentence blocks is not a page.

pack_queue.description:
What the packer is about to do, not only what it is doing. Without it a
chapter waiting to be packed looks idle.
